#4324. Disney Speedstorm - Racers tier list

Updated on November 4th, 2026 - Version: 1.20.1 - Latest Additions: Miguel Rivera, Hector Rivera, Ernesto de la Cruz

It’s pretty much a fact that Disney boasts one of the widest rosters of characters and famous franchises, enjoyed by kids and adults alike. From Sleeping Beauty to Mulan and more, there are very few places and times that the Disney vault hasn’t touched upon. So it’s no surprise that they’re making their way to mobile again…although this time in a very different, high-octane way.

Disney Speedstorm is a kart racer that features characters from across the Disney world, split into four current (and growing) factions or teams of racers. These include: Beauty and the Beast, which features characters from the film; Hercules, Mulan, Mickey & Friends, Pirates of the Caribbean, The Jungle Book, Monsters Inc., Toy Story, Walt Disney World, Lilo & Stitch, and Aladdin.

Yes, it’s quite a stacked roster, and while many (if not all) of these films are aimed towards a younger audience, we know that more than a few readers probably have a hard time letting go of their enjoyment of the Disney classics, modern and otherwise. So we’re expecting quite a large, more skill-oriented and older audience that will have all the same questions that players of other, more hardcore games may ask.

For example, what differences do the racers have between each other, and which are the best to use? Well, for differences, quite a lot actually, as it wouldn’t be a character-based roster if you didn’t have variables between them. So, in the spirit of our previous coverage of many other games, we’ve brought together a brief tier list ranking all the characters in Disney Speedstorm, from the beauties to the beasts and deciding just where they fall on a firm ranking. Right out of the (Disney) vault Racers have different stats, including Top Speed, Acceleration, Handling, Boost and Combat. However, for the sake of argument, we’re going to take into account their subjective performance and aggregate against where they’ve placed elsewhere. It’s also worth noting that many players who prefer to play competitively have reportedly pursued a playstyle wherein they eschew upgrades or pit members (which are selectable upgrades that boost performance), so there’s a lot of debate about whether or not character difference matters for more casual play.

So, with our Disney Speedstorm tier list, you can get to grips with the huge variety of iconic characters taking to the racing circuit.

Without further ado, let’s get into it, starting with…

Characters in this tier are, obviously, top of the leaderboard when it comes to performance. Although stats make a huge difference, we’ve aggregated their placement against the general opinion and what we’ve seen from playing ourselves. Elizabeth Swann, for example, takes this spot for her consistent placement in the top tier; however, we have seen her drop in some estimations as more characters are added, with those like Buzz Lightyear shooting to the top consistently since his release.

It’s no surprise that Gaston places so consistently high. As the lyric goes, “No-one fights like Gaston”, and his skill, Trophy Hunting, essentially means he can use his special ability to knock out opponents consistently. And if you’ve got good aim, you won’t need to worry about how long it takes to refresh.

He also provides a pretty good example of what this tier is about. These characters possess exciting and varied skills and abilities that mark them out from the rest of the pack. However, for whatever reason, they still don’t rank highly in the reception of players. This could be simply because they don’t work out competitively, or that their abilities are done better by other characters in their faction.

It’s ironic that Disney’s poster boy is in this tier; however, it suits the fact that Mickey is somewhat of a difficult starting character. Especially due to his low top speed, which means that he can end up lagging behind other racers. However, we still place him fairly high because - well - he’s Mickey Mouse, and because the fact you’ll probably end up playing through the single-player missions starring him and soon upgrading this racer means that you won’t have to cope with his lacklustre starting stats for too long.

However, Mickey does have one crippling weakness, which is the fact his special ability - Trailblazer - not only boosts you…but also all the other racers behind you! It’s quite charitable, but not exactly the best if you’re hoping to leave other racers in the dust.

Getting down to the C tier, we have racers that are simply lacking in most departments. As we stated at the start, it’s difficult to nail down truly bad characters in any racer, as your skill is a crucial part of the performance. However, some of these characters possess abilities or drawbacks that are simply too prominent to ignore.

Hercules, for example, suffers one decisive drawback in his character, which is that his special ability not only actively aids his opponents, like Mickey’s does, but also makes them invulnerable! The only saving grace here is, of course, that this only applies to racers who follow the trail left by his ability, which means those up ahead won’t benefit. But it is a significant drawback, regardless.

Fortunately for the characters relegated to the bottom of this Disney Speedstorm tier list, there are no truly bad characters, as any of them can be relatively decent under the right circumstances. However, these characters lack the potential and high performance that marks out those in the upper tiers. Don’t fret if your personal favourite is in this tier, as you can still play them with reasonable expectations to take home some victories. Just don’t expect to breeze your way to victory, and be ready to work for your wins. As of the first version of this list, there’s fortunately only one character who’s had a cold reception across the board.

If you don’t know who Figment is, we don’t blame you, as he’s quite a deep cut even for Disney superfans. He’s actually the mascot for the Epcot attraction in Walt Disney World. Certainly, he’s not as popular as the other characters on this list and has had quite a muted reaction both competitively and casually. And it’s no surprise given his poor stats are balanced out only by a somewhat useful special ability in Spark of Imagination that can obscure other racer’s vision, but requires you to be in close proximity to a large number of them to get maximum utility - and only a short speed boost to compensate for the poor placement you’d need to either intentionally or accidentally be in to use it.

As always, we have the fans over at the Disney Speedstorm wiki to thank for having the information on each individual racer’s abilities and stats readily accessible. Their list has been invaluable and provides an easy way to compare racers out of the game, as well as some info on the trivia and easter eggs you can find on the characters’ racing suits and elsewhere. Thanks in part to a surprisingly robust character roster and equally exciting scenery and references to popular Disney films, there’s also a vibrant and thriving fan community to engage with when it comes to Disney Speedstorm.

Since you've lasted this long, we also have a Defense Derby tier list, as you're an avid fan of cars, obviously.

#4323. NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles

NASA's Perseverance rover has reached an impressive new milestone, traveling farther across another world than any vehicle before it. On Sol 2006 (Oct. 11, 2026), the rover's total driving distance reached 45.22 kilometers (28.10 miles), establishing a new record for travel on another celestial body. The achievement was even recognized by Guinness World Records, which presented a commemorative plaque to Perseverance's engineering twin on Earth.

The rover had actually come close to breaking the record about two months earlier. On Sol 1947, Perseverance was just 200 meters short of the milestone, a distance it could have covered in a single trip using its Autonomous Navigation (AutoNav) system.

But reaching the record was not the team's immediate priority. Perseverance was exploring an area filled with scientifically valuable ancient rock formations, so it spent weeks making short trips between locations to examine exposed rock surfaces. These investigations included grinding away thin layers of rock and conducting detailed measurements up close. Once the scientific work was complete, the rover resumed its journey and soon surpassed the previous distance record.

"Two months ago, (Perseverance) sat about 200 meters away from the milestone, a distance easily achievable with a single drive... However, the rover found itself in a very scientifically interesting area and spent time (investigating) ancient rock outcrops. When Perseverance was finally ready to move on to a new site, it sailed past the record."

How NASA Improved Perseverance's Driving Capabilities

Covering more than 28 miles on Mars has required Perseverance to overcome difficult terrain while testing new approaches to robotic driving. Its journeys through tightly packed boulder fields and across steep hillsides have given NASA engineers valuable experience, helping them improve the rover's ability to navigate hazardous landscapes.

To expand what Perseverance can safely handle, engineers conducted thousands of computer simulations and adjusted several operating limits. The rover can now tolerate tilts of up to 24 degrees, while the minimum clearance beneath its protective belly pan has been reduced to 20 centimeters (about 7.9 inches).

The team also introduced several important improvements to the driving system. Updated braking software helps the rover avoid collisions with rocks, and the electrical current limits for its steering motors have been nearly doubled. Engineers also added "dynamic slip tables" to its flight software, allowing the rover to better anticipate how much its wheels might slip on different surfaces.

Another technique involves driving across slopes in ways that help keep the wheels securely positioned on exposed bedrock. Together, these changes allow Perseverance to handle challenging terrain more effectively as it continues exploring Mars.

A Mars Rover That Can Navigate Without GPS

Among the rover's most significant technological advances is a system called onboard Global Localization (GBLC). This technology gives Perseverance a way to determine its position on Mars without relying on directions from Earth.

The system uses a powerful commercial processor originally installed in the Ingenuity Helicopter Base Station. By comparing images captured from the Martian surface with pictures taken from orbit, it can calculate the rover's location in global coordinates after completing a drive (as though we had GPS on a world without it).

Knowing its position independently is a major advantage. It allows Perseverance to cover greater distances without needing people on Earth to repeatedly determine its location, potentially making future exploration faster and more efficient.

However, this approach introduced an engineering challenge. Unlike the rover's main flight computer, the additional processor was not specifically designed to withstand the intense radiation conditions on Mars. The planet has a thin atmosphere and no global magnetic field, leaving electronics exposed to radiation that can interfere with their operation.

In particular, radiation can cause "transient bit flips" that unexpectedly change information stored in computer memory, potentially disrupting software. To address this problem, engineers developed software protections that help the processor operate reliably despite the harsh environment.

The Next Frontier in Autonomous Mars Exploration

NASA is also investigating how generative AI could make the rover even more independent. As missions involve longer journeys and increasingly complex operations, the team wants to reduce the time and resources needed to plan safe routes.

The technology could help generate driving plans for the many individual segments of a longer journey, providing guidance that Perseverance's AutoNav system can use to navigate the terrain.

After traveling 45 kilometers (more than 28 miles), Perseverance has already provided engineers with extensive experience in navigating the Martian landscape. Those lessons are now shaping new technologies that could transform how robotic explorers operate on distant worlds.

And the journey is far from over. As Perseverance continues climbing higher along the rim of its Martian crater, NASA is preparing for the next major advances in autonomous exploration.

Materials provided by NASA. Original written by Vandi Verma, Chief Engineer for Robotic Operations at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4322. EA Is Closing Down Legendary Studio BioWare Amid More Job Cuts

Electronic Arts plans to eliminate roughly 400 positions in an upcoming round of job cuts, per a new report from Bloomberg, and will also be closing the doors on its long-time role-playing game maker BioWare.

Per Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, these cuts represent about three percent of EA's total staff, and roughly 50 at BioWare. A letter sent to staff today from EA's COO David Tinson and Chief Studios Officer Cam Weber said that they've taken a "hard look at our business" and will cut projects, including the next Mass Effect.

"As we focus on these larger opportunities, we've had a small team at BioWare working on early-development for Mass Effect," the letter reads. "We've made the decision not to move forward with this development, which means we’re closing the studio and our Edmonton workspace. BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly."

Sports, shooters (like Apex Legends), and Star Wars (including the next Jedi title) will continue apace at Electronic Arts. The publisher also has a new Iron Man game in the works, and plans are in the works for more Battlefield, as well as a new collaboration between Respawn and DICE. The staff letter also suggests a planned Sims game will be put on ice in favor of another venture, and that while Skate development will continue, EA will downsize the team working on it.

EA was fully acquired earlier this year by a number of investor groups, including Silver Lake, Affinity Partners, and the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, taking the publicly traded company private. In its announcement at the time, EA chairman and CEO Andrew Wilson said, "We're entering this next chapter from a position of strength with partners who share our vision and ambition. Together, we'll invest boldly, accelerate innovation, and build the next generation of games and experiences for the hundreds of millions of players and fans who inspire us every day."

A statement from BioWare posted to social media shared the closure as well, highlighting the list of games it has brought to life: Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect, and Anthem. The team's focus now, per the statement, is on supporting one another through this transition.

"What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember," the statement reads. "These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with the characters, and made these worlds your own. From all of us at BioWare, thank you for being the most meaningful part of our story."

BioWare has been known throughout its history for exactly that: an undoubtedly legendary run of role-playing games where choice, characters, and moments matter. From the early era of D&D-driven adventures to leading the pack in console RPG development with KOTOR, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age, few Western RPG studios boast the legacy BioWare had.

Still, BioWare often sailed on troubled waters. The underwhelming releases of Mass Effect: Andromeda and Anthem tarnished the studio's pristine image in the eyes of some fans. Dragon Age: The Veilguard, the studio's most recent—and final—game was generally better received by critics, but spent a decade in development turmoil. Internal strife over the making of these massive RPGs was the subject of frequent reporting. The term "BioWare magic," referring to how the studio's games would finally come together in the twilight hours of development, became a sticking point as the years went on.

There is no denying, though, how BioWare has played an active hand in molding the role-playing genre over the years. Even a recitation of past works doesn't feel accurate to the impact; the influence of Mass Effect and Dragon Age alone is something we still see ripples of today. Even as other studios have taken up the torch and put their own spin on companion-driven, choices-matter stories, there is still an innate sense of "BioWare" that's hard to remove from those interactions and moments.

Layoffs have become distressingly commonplace, as cuts to legendary teams are announced at a never-ending pace. But to break news writing decorum, I had always hoped, throughout years of working in this industry, that I wouldn't ever have to eulogize a studio like BioWare. A place that shaped my own dive into video games, and I'm sure did the same for many, many others. A roof under which developers worked long hours to craft stories we'd carry with us for years. I'm thankful for that, and hope those affected find somewhere new that's rewarding of their talents.

#4321. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4319. Extra weight may be aging your brain faster than you think

Carrying excess weight may affect more than physical health. New research from the University of Georgia suggests that having a higher body mass index may also speed up cognitive decline, potentially causing memory and thinking abilities to deteriorate more quickly with age.

Some cognitive changes are a natural part of getting older. Remembering information, thinking clearly, and processing new details can become more difficult over time. For healthy adults, however, these changes are usually relatively mild and develop gradually.

The new findings suggest that excess body weight may accelerate this process. Researchers found that people with higher body mass index (BMI) experienced faster declines in memory, overall cognitive performance, and executive functioning. These abilities are essential for everyday activities such as concentrating, planning, organizing tasks, and regulating emotions.

To investigate the connection, the research team analyzed data from a nationally representative study that tracked more than 8,200 adults over age 50 for 24 years.

Higher BMI Linked to Faster Cognitive Decline

The results revealed a consistent relationship between body weight and cognitive health. Each one-point increase in BMI was associated with a faster rate of cognitive decline, suggesting that even relatively small differences in body weight could matter over time.

The association was strongest at the eighth year of the study, and adults older than 65 showed the most pronounced effects.

Despite the concerning findings, researchers also identified a potentially encouraging opportunity to protect brain health. Managing body weight may help slow cognitive decline, with possible benefits becoming apparent within just two years.

"We found that if people managed their weight, they could significantly lower their rate of cognitive decline in just two years," said Suhang Song, the study's lead author and an assistant professor at the University of Georgia's College of Public Health. "That makes BMI one of the most easily modifiable risk factors when it comes to aging well."

How Excess Weight May Affect the Aging Brain

Obesity, generally defined as a BMI of 30 or higher, has been associated with poorer brain health. However, scientists are still working to understand exactly why carrying excess body weight may interfere with memory and other cognitive abilities.

Several biological processes could help explain the connection. Excess weight may promote inflammation, impair blood circulation, and contribute to insulin resistance. Together, these changes could increase the likelihood of cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and other forms of dementia.

The findings are particularly relevant given how widespread obesity has become in the United States. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, approximately two in five Americans meet the criteria for obesity when BMI is used as the sole measure.

Some scientists argue that BMI alone does not provide a complete picture of obesity. They support a broader definition that also considers waist measurements and medical conditions associated with excess weight. Using those additional criteria, the estimated proportion of Americans classified as having obesity rises to 75%.

Weight Management Could Help Protect Brain Health

The potential connection between obesity and cognitive decline is especially concerning as dementia becomes increasingly common. More than 7 million Americans currently live with dementia, and researchers expect that number to double by 2050.

Although the study does not establish that excess weight directly causes cognitive decline, its findings highlight body weight as a potentially important factor in maintaining cognitive health. Because weight can be managed, researchers believe it could offer an opportunity to reduce the risk of worsening memory and thinking abilities as people grow older.

"There are no cures for dementia," Song said, "which is why it is critical to identify and address any modifiable risk factors we can find to prevent it."

The research was published in the Journal of Neurology. Coauthors from the University of Georgia College of Public Health include Meng Hsuan Sung, Zhuo Chen, Janani Rajbhandari, Grace Bagwell Adams, Mahmud Khan, Ye Shen, and Xiao Song. Qianhui Xu and Xia Song also contributed to the study.

Materials provided by University of Georgia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4318. 10 Action-Adventure Games That Are Unexpected Masterpieces

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

The action-adventure genre is one of the broadest in the entire video game industry, encompassing countless experiences ranging from stealth and hack-and-slash to horror and beat 'em ups.

Thanks to this broad definition, countless masterpieces fall under its umbrella, including many that, unfortunately, haven't achieved the popularity they deserve due to fierce competition.

Even within the realm of major blockbusters, not all underrated titles are obscure indie games—there are games that have fallen just short of mainstream success, though I'm here to help rectify that.

So, in order to shed light on some lesser-known campaigns that haven't yet cemented their undeniable excellence in the collective consciousness, I invite you to explore this list of ten action-adventure games that are unexpected masterpieces.

As the least recognized work from Tango Gameworks, a studio that has certainly gifted us with numerous magnificent journeys, Ghostwire: Tokyo stands out among the games with the greatest disparity between its quality and its fame.

Boasting one of the finest atmospheres crafted this decade, wandering the streets of Shibuya, soaring across rooftops, and taking down the most terrifying yokai imaginable is, by far, one of my highlights of the decade.

Whether in stealth or direct magical combat, tackling one of its turbulent side quests or hunting for collectibles, the game strikes an outstanding balance between making each mechanic satisfying while still maintaining a constant sense of terror in its setting.

As far as first-person games go, Ghostwire: Tokyo is part of the most immersive, rewarding, and distinctive I've played this generation, which is saying something considering the titans with which it shares category.

As the years have gone by, games that adhere to the Metroidvania philosophy have become one of my greatest obsessions, which inevitably led me to fall in love with Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo.

Its ability to capture the nostalgia of the Game Boy Advance era while boasting the refined design and execution of modern products demonstrates its creators' immeasurable talent, who also imbued it with an impressive thematic personality.

The critiques of various strategic production industries resonate with our current times, while in the process, the game leverages the yoyo as a central gameplay element to make traversal, combat, exploration, and customization an absolute delight that's also pretty unique.

Pipistrello and the Cursed Yoyo is among the finest indie titles I've enjoyed in the last couple of years, and anything other than recognizing it as brilliant is to underestimate its potential.

If you're interested in unfairly criticized titles, I recommend checking out these ten underrated action-adventure games that were badly reviewed.

As someone who didn't experience the franchise's heyday, Shinobi: Art of Vengeance not only caught me completely off guard, but I can think of very few resurrections that have felt so powerful.

The absolute masterwork of action and platforming that this title is results in frankly mind-blowing sequences, flowing seamlessly between both dimensions to deliver a thrilling adventure that doesn't let you breathe for a second.

As you unlock combos, powers, and movement abilities, you encounter an ever-increasing series of challenges that push the game's mechanics to their limits, which are meticulously refined to ensure you have complete control over every pixel.

Few titles in 2025 felt as satisfying to complete 100%, so Shinobi: Art of Vengeance stands as a masterfully unexpected example that, when you don't know what to do with your old IPs, outsourcing to an indie studio to work on them is the best possible idea.

The Legend of Zelda's heirs number in the hundreds of thousands, but that didn't stop Death's Door from emerging as one of its most intelligent and charismatic great-great-grandchildren.

The game perfectly understands the enjoyment that lies in discovery and exploration through iteration, inviting us on a diverse adventure with plenty of colorful biomes, enemies, characters, and circumstances that evoke all kinds of emotions.

Curiosity, fear, happiness, sadness, worry... The title silently manages a multitude of emotions both thematically and in its gameplay, limiting progression to allow for exploration of its expansive world at a prodigious pace.

When discussing isometric titles that combine action, platforming, and puzzles in the best possible way, Death's Door is at the description's forefront, though it's the ease and finesse with which it achieves this that's truly unexpected.

Castlevania is a series that went through some difficult years after the turn of the century, and it wasn't until Castlevania: Lords of Shadow arrived that the IP unexpectedly found some relief amidst so many setbacks, astonishingly becoming the best-selling game in the entire IP.

MercurySteam crafted one of the most beautiful and satisfying hack-and-slash games in the genre's history, finally adapting the saga's formula perfectly to 3D without losing an ounce of its core identity.

The whip feels better than ever, as do the movement mechanics, the puzzles, and the progression systems, all enhanced in the best possible way thanks to a magnificently crafted story and characters that keep you on the edge of your seat until the very last second.

Castlevania: Lords of Shadow completely forgoes being conceptually innovative, but the sacrifice, given it guaranteed us an extremely excellent title in all its facets, was totally worth it even when nobody was betting on such a resounding success.

If you enjoy discovering incredible titles without proper recognition, I recommend these ten best action-adventure games forgotten by time.

In the years when God of War slowed down, and Devil May Cry practically disappeared, a third icon emerged from absolutely nowhere to keep the hack-and-slash genre alive (with Bayonetta's permission): Darksiders.

Drawing inspiration from both Santa Monica Studio's work and The Legend of Zelda, Vigil Games crafted a splendidly elaborate tale and setting within Judeo-Christian mythology, one of the least explored in the video game industry.

Giant bosses based on satisfying gimmicks, varied and refreshing puzzles that make the most of War's arsenal and movement capabilities, phenomenal art design for both environments and enemies... It's the complete package.

That the company's first title would be such a presentation of knowledge in the genre's fundamentals was unforeseen even for the team itself, but much more for the hundreds of thousands who, like me, stumbled upon Darksiders by chance and have been hooked ever since.

Returning to the topic of franchises forced to reinvent themselves to adapt to modern times, not even the most optimistic projections for the Tomb Raider reboot could have predicted the absolute brilliance it would become.

Going back to Lara Croft's origins resulted in one of the quintessential action-adventure games of the entire generation, achieving an astonishing symphony of survival mechanics, realistic yet compelling gunplay, and simply fantastic settings and stories.

Each set piece surpasses the last, and the spectacular scenery contrasts perfectly with the brutal and tense story the legendary archaeologist faces, all while possessing the intriguing premise of not yet being the intrepid adventurer we all know, but rather a young, still-innocent graduate.

From concept to execution, Tomb Raider is a tapestry of sound decisions that, among other things, reminded Uncharted fans that Nathan Drake only managed to run because Lara Croft walked first.

I know that nowadays we're used to indie masterpieces being released every couple of months, but back in the day, before that was the norm, Hyper Light Drifter arrived like a hurricane of grandeur.

Taking Dark Souls' harshness, non-linearity, and disorientation, Heart Machine assembled an adventure that is both cryptic and captivating, where the gameplay and narrative direction are entirely in the player's hands.

Where to go and why are questions that only the user can answer through exploration, embarking on an intense and introspective journey where bosses and secrets abound, motivating us to explore every last corner of its silent world.

Along with gorgeous pixel art, a remarkable sound design, and a simple yet perfect gameplay loop, Hyper Light Drifter built a castle with just a few blocks, a feat reserved only for the greatest.

If you're looking for modern games to get lost in, I recommend the ten best adventure games of the 2020s (so far).

The reviews for Asura's Wrath were so scathing that it took me a decade to finally deign to play it, and the sheer shock of finishing it in tears when the credits rolled was beyond words.

Yes, every single one of the comments regarding its poor gameplay was, is, and will be correct, since it's a beat 'em up where the best parts of the gameplay are the on-rails shooting and quick-time events, and that doesn't exactly reflect well on a title of this genre.

Regardless, when you have such an incredible plot, abundant with charismatic characters, memorable scenes, robust mythology, and eccentrically immeasurable cinematics, I couldn't care less that every encounter boils down to mashing the attack button a hundred times a second.

The intercosmic scale that Asura's Wrath handles in its presentation and spectacle is monumental, unique, and emotional enough to overlook its mediocre mechanics, being the only case in the entire genre where it's a masterpiece even without being fun in the traditional sense.

Bucking the trend in the genre, whose disdain for stealth became evident in the last decade, Arkane Studios made a tremendous statement in 2012 with Dishonored's release.

Coming from another underrated gem, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, the studio embraced the lingering force of immersive sims and materialized it into a project that excels as both a stealth game and an action-adventure game.

Boasting some of the best level design in video game history, along with a story that evolves based on the player's actions rather than dialogue choices, Dishonored is one of the century's defining power fantasies.

Between Dunwall's perfect setting, the outstanding array of gadgets and powers that allow for creative and expansive use of stealth and violence, and the majestic musical pieces that accompany us, it's clear that the love for stealth games will never die as long as this IP remains available.

Years go by, and I still wonder if the genre has enough strength to produce a title that surpasses Dishonored, but for now, it remains on the throne without any concern about being replaced.

In this list, we'll discuss our picks for the best action-adventure games that go beyond a hundred hours, from RPGs to known open-world titles.

Share your take with fellow players. Keep it constructive, relevant, and respectful.

#4317. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4316. Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation

For decades, one of the most common recommendations for lowering high blood pressure has been simple: eat less salt. But a new scientific report suggests that this advice may be missing an equally important part of the equation.

Researchers say that increasing potassium intake, rather than focusing only on reducing sodium, could lead to better blood pressure control. By addressing both nutrients together, this approach could strengthen efforts to prevent hypertension and reduce the risk of serious cardiovascular problems.

The potential impact is enormous. High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, affects more than 1.28 billion adults worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including heart attacks and strokes. Although public health recommendations have traditionally emphasized cutting sodium, researchers now argue that getting enough potassium deserves just as much attention.

Sodium and potassium are essential minerals that help regulate fluid balance, nerve signaling, and muscle function. Both also influence blood pressure, but they affect the body in different ways.

Eating too much sodium can cause the body to retain additional fluid, increasing the pressure inside blood vessels. Potassium helps counter some of sodium's effects by supporting the kidneys in removing excess sodium through urine. It also contributes to the normal functioning of blood vessel walls, which plays an important role in maintaining healthy blood pressure.

In a new report, physicians and health experts argue that dietary recommendations should address these two minerals together. Rather than treating sodium reduction as the primary solution, they propose combining it with greater potassium consumption to achieve stronger results.

"It is time to view dietary interventions holistically because food components interact and physiology is integrative across systems," said Naomi Fukagawa, M.D. Ph.D., professor of medicine emerita at the Robert Larner, M.D. College of Medicine at the University of Vermont and first author on the report. "Growing evidence shows that increasing dietary potassium as well as reducing sodium intake work together to better manage hypertension."

A Major Rethink of Blood Pressure Guidelines

The report, published in the peer-reviewed American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, was supported by the IAFNS Sodium in Food and Health Implications Committee.

The researchers examined the scientific evidence underlying current sodium and potassium recommendations, along with practical ways to reduce sodium consumption and increase potassium intake. They also explored the obstacles to implementing these changes and identified areas where additional research and updated public health policies could help improve outcomes.

One of the central concerns is that many people consume too much sodium while getting nowhere near enough potassium. Both dietary patterns can contribute to elevated blood pressure, making them important targets for prevention and treatment.

Despite widespread efforts to encourage people to limit salt, average sodium consumption continues to exceed recommended levels. Meanwhile, potassium intake remains "far below optimal levels in both developed and developing nations," according to the authors.

This imbalance suggests that focusing primarily on what people should eat less of may be overlooking an important opportunity to improve cardiovascular health by encouraging them to consume more of a beneficial nutrient.

Potassium is naturally present in many familiar foods, including fruits, vegetables, legumes, and dairy products. Bananas, potatoes, beans, leafy greens, and yogurt are examples of foods that can help increase potassium intake.

Another possibility is replacing some sodium chloride, the main ingredient in ordinary table salt, with potassium salts. These substitutes can help reduce sodium while simultaneously increasing potassium, potentially addressing both dietary goals at once.

However, creating these products presents challenges for food manufacturers. Adding too much potassium salt can produce an unpleasant metallic taste, limiting how much can be used without affecting flavor. Manufacturers must therefore find a balance that improves nutritional content while keeping foods appealing to consumers.

Increasing potassium is also not appropriate for everyone. People with kidney disease or those taking certain medications may have difficulty regulating potassium levels, so potassium supplements and potassium-based salt substitutes should be used with medical guidance when these concerns apply.

A New Strategy for Fighting High Blood Pressure

The researchers emphasize that reducing sodium remains essential. Their proposal is not to abandon existing advice, but to expand it by recognizing that potassium intake is another major factor in blood pressure regulation.

The authors conclude that "dietary sodium reduction is a foundational strategy for hypertension prevention and management. However, new evidence supports a broadening of the current approach that focuses solely on sodium reduction and provides equal emphasis on increasing potassium intake."

For the more than one billion people living with hypertension, this shift in thinking could have significant implications. Instead of concentrating almost exclusively on reducing salt, future dietary recommendations may increasingly emphasize the combined benefits of consuming less sodium and more potassium.

The underlying message is straightforward: better blood pressure control may depend not only on what people remove from their diets, but also on what they add.

Materials provided by University of Vermont. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4315. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a big game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.
